Il y a une atténuation modérée des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémorotibial interne, sans atteinte transfixiante. Il y a de petits ostéophytes marginaux.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] active male unable to exercise due to right knee pain on exertion. Lateral right knee pain.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.    
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact and appears unremarkable. There is mild edema in the suprapatellar fat pad. This finding is mild, equivocal and is nonspecific but may correlate clinically with dynamic and symptomatic impingement of the fat pad.

The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and unremarkable. Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained.

The TT-TG distance measures about 9 mm, within normal limits.

The lateral meniscus is intact and appears unremarkable. Articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The medial meniscus is intact and unremarkable. Articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament and medial collateral ligament are intact and appear unremarkable.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact. There is a trace of fluid deep to the IT band but no evidence of synovitis to suggest IT band syndrome.

Fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and biceps femoris tendon are intact.

There is a trace Baker's cyst. No significant knee effusion.

There is a small parameniscal ganglion cyst demonstrated arising near the posterior root attachment of medial meniscus extending around the posterior cruciate ligament measuring about 1.3 x 1.0 x 0.4 cm. No associated meniscal tear is seen to account for this ganglion cyst.

INTERPRETATION: 

No evidence of internal derangement.

Small ganglion cyst in the popliteal fossa.

Mild edema in the suprapatellar fat pad, nonspecific.

No definite cause for lateral joint pain is identified.

Il y a aussi un léger amincissement du cartilage à la partie latérale de la trochlée du fémur. La rotule démontre une légère subluxation latérale. Il y a aussi œdème au niveau de la partie supéro-latérale du pad graisseux infra-rotulien entre le tendon rotulien et le condyle fémoral externe.

Le cartilage du compartiment interne et externe est préservé. Les ménisques sont sans particularité. Autrement le ligament croisé antérieur, le ligament croisé postérieur, le mécanisme des extenseurs, le ligament collatéral interne, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et tendon du poplité, le biceps fémoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette ilio-tibiale sont sans particularité.

Conclusion :

Œdème au niveau du pad graisseux suggestif d’un syndrome de friction (patellar tendon lateral femoral condyle friction syndrome). Il y a aussi changements dégénératifs au niveau patellofémoral. La combinaison des trouvailles est suggestif d’une biomécanique anormale au niveau patellofémoral.

Indication: Right knee swelling rule out internal derangement.

FINDINGS:

Large knee effusion with extensive synovitis. No significant Baker's cyst. There is thickening of the medial and lateral plica.

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Severe chondrosis involving the femoral patellar compartment with complete delamination of the lateral facet of the patella and subchondral edema. There is area of full-thickness fissuring and significant thinning of the lateral trochlear surface. Chondrosis is milder on the medial facet of the patella. Lateral subluxation of the patella in regards to the trochlea.
Extensor mechanism appears unremarkable. Hoffa's fat pad unremarkable.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Moderate severe chondrosis with area of full-thickness cartilage delamination without subchondral edema or cyst. Intermediate signal within the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with maceration. No discrete tear. Small meniscal flounce at the anterior body.
Medial collateral ligament intact. Portions visualize of the pes anserine unremarkable. Mild semimembranosus tendinosis.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT :
Mild chondrosis. No discrete meniscal tear. Popliteus tendon lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris unremarkable. Proximal tibiofibular joint unremarkable. Iliotibial band unremarkable.

INTERCONDYLAR COMPARTMENT:
Anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament intact. Small intercondylar notch ganglion cysts measuring 1.5 x 1.4 x 2.4 cm.

Main neurovascular structures reveal visualized are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:
1. Severe osteoarthritis involving the femoropatellar compartment and moderate to severe osteoarthritis to the medial compartment and milder chondrosis to the lateral compartment.

2. Large effusions with extensive synovitis associated. Considering the extent of the synovitis could inflammatory arthritis be associated? Although the OA as a more mechanical distribution.

INDICATION: Left knee injury [Date] with persistent pain on flexion. Ultrasound showed severely thickened and hypoechoic posterior cruciate ligament (report attached)/ ? PCL strain/tear

TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The quadriceps tendon is intact. The patellar tendon is intact.

Articular irregularity and signal heterogeneity of the patellar cartilage, and underlying marrow edema overall suggestive of severe chondromalacia patellae.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. The tibial aspect of the posterior cruciate ligament is relatively thickened with focal intermediate signal thickening suggestive of scar tissue, and suggestive of previously low-grade partial tear. No posterior tibial translation.

The anterior horn medial meniscus is slightly extruded 3 mm beyond the tibial plateau. No medial meniscal tear is identified. Mild chondrosis medial tibiofemoral compartment.

The lateral meniscus is intact without evidence of tear. Mild chondrosis lateral tibiofemoral compartment.

No significant knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Bone contusion anterior tibia, just lateral to the tibial tubercle. Mild prepatellar soft tissue swelling.

INTERPRETATION: 

- Findings suggestive of previous posterior cruciate ligament low-grade partial tear. No abnormal tibial translation.
- Severe chondromalacia patellae. Mild chondrosis within the medial and lateral tibiofemoral compartments.
- Bone contusion anterior tibia just lateral to the tibial tubercle.
